rationale: The hypothesis posits that autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder 73 (OMIM #620450) is driven by missense variants clustering in conserved TAF homology or histone-fold domains acting via a dominant-negative or loss-of-function mechanism, while truncating variants have variable penetrance or severity. However, the foundational cohort defining this disorder (Janssen et al., 2022) established that autosomal dominant TAF4-related neurodevelopmental disorder (T4NDD) is specifically caused by de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF / truncating) variants in all 8 investigated probands. The phenotypic triad of intellectual disability, behavioral anomalies, and facial dysmorphism is directly attributed to heterozygous pLoF variants rather than a domain-specific missense clustering or dominant-negative mechanism.

evidence.text: A clinical study identified eight individuals with a novel neurodevelopmental disorder (T4NDD, OMIM #620450), all harboring de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 rather than domain-clustered missense variants.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD). Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms. We propose TAF4 as a novel dominant disease gene for NDD, and coin this novel disorder 'TAF4-related NDD' (T4NDD).

new_directions.question_text: Are there any pathogenic missense variants in TAF4 that produce an overlapping or distinct syndromic neurodevelopmental phenotype through dominant-negative mechanisms?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether missense alterations in specific TAF4 functional domains (such as the TAFH or histone-fold domains) lead to clinical disease or are largely tolerated/unrelated to OMIM #620450 will clarify the functional tolerance of the protein.

new_directions.question_text: What are the specific distinguishing facial dysmorphisms and neurobehavioral profiles in TAF4 haploinsufficiency compared to other TFIID subunit disorders (e.g., TAF1, TAF2, TAF6)?
new_directions.rationale: Comparative morphometric and behavioral phenotyping across TFIID-related 'TAF-opathies' is necessary to evaluate whether clinical features alone can distinguish TAF4-related NDD without exome or genome sequencing.
